new.analysis:
**Your first week back went exactly as it should.** You did three walk-runs of 15 minutes each, all at effort 3/10 and pain 0/10, and the shin stayed quiet. Your average heart rate was 121 to 123 and stayed in zones 1 and 2, and you did both physio sessions.

**I'm starting from about 15 minutes of running a week.** Your splits suggest 1 minute of running and 2 minutes of walking, repeated five times in each session. If you ran a different pattern, tell me and I'll adjust.

**Next week adds about 10 percent, and only one session changes.** Your weekly running goes from 15 to 16 minutes, and your longest bout goes from 1 minute to 1 minute 30 seconds. Bone adapts more slowly than fitness does, so feeling strong is not a reason to skip ahead.

**The step is on Saturday because Sunday is a rest day.** Sunday morning will then show clearly how the shin took the longer bouts. If all three runs stay at 0/10 and the mornings are quiet, the week after can use the longer bouts in more sessions.

**Pain decides the next step, not how good the running feels.** Any ache, even one that settles, starts the four-week pain-free count again. Pain above 3/10, or pain that is worse the next morning, means repeating or shortening the last session.

**Mid-October is probably too soon for 30 minutes without walking.** If every week is pain-free, adding about 10 percent a week gets you roughly this far:

| Week | Running minutes in the week |
| --- | --- |
| Sep 14 – 20 | 16 |
| Sep 21 – 27 | 18 |
| Sep 28 – Oct 4 | 20 |
| Oct 5 – 11 | 22 |
| Oct 12 – 18 | 24 |

One 30-minute run would be more than your whole week's running by mid-October. December is a more realistic target, though your physio may have their own view on how fast to build.

**It makes sense to feel nervous, and the plan keeps each step small enough that you can trust it.** One clean week is a real start. A few more like it will tell you far more than any single run.

safetyCallouts.title: Know when to stop and call your physio.
safetyCallouts.body: If the shin hurts when you walk, at rest or at night, or an ache is still there the next day, stop running and contact your physio before your next session.
